analysis.title: Raymond James Investment Strategy daily, Friday October 30, 2026: Microsoft bond deal, Communication Services bear market, 3Q26 GDP
key_insights: Google's slowing search revenue pushed the S&P 500 Communication Services sector down 6.6% on 10/29, its worst day since 2022. The sector is more than 20% below its recent high, the steepest decline of any sector.

Two other pressures hit the Communication Services sector in recent weeks. Rising hyperscaler capex has fueled AI financing concerns, and SpaceX's reported pursuit of access to 80,000 cell sites has raised worries about telecom competition.

Raymond James says the sector includes some AI beneficiaries but continues to prefer Technology for exposure to the AI megatrend. The report asks whether the drop is a buying opportunity and does not recommend buying the sector.

Microsoft sold a $25b bond, its first offering since 2017, and reportedly drew $115b of investor demand. This lifts year-to-date issuance by the top five hyperscalers to about $254b, including non-USD deals.

Year-to-date US investment grade corporate issuance has passed 2020's record and is approaching $2T. Treasuries rallied despite the heavy supply, which eased concerns that corporate and government borrowing may crowd each other out.
Massive AI capex remains a key driver of issuance, though spending is likely to moderate as the investment cycle matures.

US real GDP grew 3.4% annualized in 3Q26, driven by consumer spending and business capital investment. Equipment capex rose 20.9%, reflecting the data center buildout and the related modernization of the electric grid. The trade deficit was a sizable drag on reported growth.
Headline PCE inflation cooled from 5.0% in 2Q to 2.1% in 3Q, which supported the Fed's decision this week to hold rates steady.

The ECB held its policy rate at 2.5% after hikes in June and September, and the Bank of Japan held at 1.25% after two hikes this year. Both were in line with consensus. The Bank of Canada raised its rate 25 bps to 2.5%, its first hike since July 2023.
The Bank of England is the only G7 central bank that has not hiked in 2026, and markets expect it to hike on November 5.

Gold is slightly above its July lows, while silver and platinum fell this week to their lowest levels of 2026. Cobalt and lithium are also at year-to-date lows. The report says precious metals are less attractive with bond yields near multi-decade highs.
Lower metals prices reduce input costs for a wide range of manufacturers, and some of the savings could be passed on to consumers.

In the 10/29 close, the S&P 500 fell 0.3% to 7,720 (+12.8% YTD) and the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.4% to 29,403 (+16.4% YTD). The Russell 2000 rose 1.0% to 2,859 and the 10-year Treasury yield was 4.98%, down 6 bps. Pre-market futures at 07:47 ET were S&P 500 -1.0% and Nasdaq 100 -2.5%.

sector_views.rationale: Raymond James continues to prefer Technology for exposure to the AI megatrend over Communication Services.
The sector is in a bear market after a 6.6% one-day drop. It includes some AI beneficiaries, but the report prefers Technology for AI exposure and does not call the drop a buy.

earnings_insights: Alphabet (Google) reported slowing search revenue, which drove the S&P 500 Communication Services sector down 6.6% on 10/29. The report gives no EPS or revenue figures and no consensus comparison.

Reflects the data center buildout and the related modernization of the electric grid.
Cooler inflation supported the Fed's decision this week to hold rates steady.
